name: Posterior Labral Tear of the Shoulder
tags: posterior labral tear of the shoulder
definition: Tear of the posterior glenoid labrum, often associated with posterior instability, repetitive loading or trauma.

investigations.principle: MRI or MR arthrography is used when a clinically meaningful posterior labral lesion is suspected.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, ligament, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent instability or mechanical symptoms may require arthroscopic repair.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa-Sandhi/Snayu phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Tear of the posterior glenoid labrum, often associated with posterior instability, repetitive loading or trauma.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected serious infection, airway/vascular symptoms, unreduced dislocation or other listed red flags.
